title: Switch Off All the Lights

concept.title: Decide only the first row; the other rows are forced
body: A square grid of lamps is on or off. Pressing a lamp toggles it **and its up to four neighbours**. We want to switch all lamps off with the fewest presses. Pressing a lamp twice has no effect and the order of presses does not matter, so a solution is just a **set** of pressed lamps: `2^(n*n)` sets, far too many for 64 lamps.

The trick: look at the first row only. Choose which lamps of the first row are pressed (`2^n` choices). After that, a lamp `(0, j)` of the first row can still be changed only by a press at `(1, j)` in the second row. So the presses of the second row are **forced**: press `(1, j)` exactly when the lamp `(0, j)` is still on. In general, press `(i, j)` exactly when the lamp `(i - 1, j)` is on. All rows are determined by the first row; at the end check that the last row is dark.

The whole search is `2^n` tries of `n * n` work each: for `n = 8` about 16 000 steps instead of `2^64` sets. Whenever the effect of a choice is **forced** by the earlier choices, one can enumerate only the free part, and the rest follows by calculation.

statement: An `n` by `n` grid has lamps that are on (`1`) or off (`0`). Pressing a lamp toggles that lamp and its neighbours above, below, left and right (those that exist). Print the smallest number of presses that switches all the lamps off, or `-1` if it is impossible.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has `n` characters, `0` or `1`.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of presses, or `-1`.

examples.note: One press on the middle lamp switches off the plus-shaped group: the answer is 1.

hints: A lamp pressed twice is the same as not pressed: only sets of presses matter.
Try every set of presses in the first row.
After the first row, the press of lamp (i, j) is forced: it must be pressed exactly when lamp (i - 1, j) is still on.

n = int(input())
lamps = [input().strip() for _ in range(n)]

explanation: Only the presses of the first row are chosen (`2^n` ways); each later press is forced by the lamp above it. If the last row is dark at the end, the number of presses is a candidate, and the smallest candidate is the answer.
